what: Behind the panel, three.js renders 23 weightless floating objects (keycap, hand, headphones, balloon dog — basic shapes) twice, one raw pass and one face-direction pass, and composites them — outside the window it is paper (--kf-bg) with pencil lines (--kf-line) drawn only where face direction bends, inside the window it is the raw render on a black stage (--kf-contrast-bg) with a grid wall. Objects are pulled toward the center only by 0.0003×distance (up to 5), and within radius 7 of a moving mouse they are pushed by 100.8×(1−distance/7) (force ±0.5, mass .025, damping .1). Hovering the window enlarges the window hole 1.2x (.5s power2.out), and with fx:open it opens to the whole panel in 1.15s power4.inOut, leaving only the raw render

options.count · count-narrow: Number of items, default 23 · 10 below a board width of 820px
options.scale: Object size scale, default 1.55 (about 1/6 of screen height)
options.reach: Mouse influence radius (world units, plane 25 in front of the camera), default 7
options.grow: Hole scale when a hand is placed on the window, default 1.2
options.open: Duration in seconds for the window to open and close across the whole panel via fx:open·fx:close, default 1.15
options.fx:open · fx:close: Send to a panel and the window opening expands to the whole panel (fires fx:opened when fully open) · closes back to the window
options.[data-fx-part=window]: (if present) window where the raw version shows — this element sets the press spot, size and corners (border-radius). If absent, the whole panel is pencil-lined paper

note: The original solves box collisions too with cannon.js 0.6.2, but the part uses only three, integrating the same forces and damping by hand and resolving overlap only around the ball. Object shapes are our basic primitives, so the lines are simpler than the original models. One WebGL context per panel, so don’t place several on one screen

from.where: shared.js stage · index.html Hero window (.px-portal, min(520px,56vw) · 1.55:1 · 30px) — the Contact page shows the full paper without the window
